content.title: Everything Matt Rhule said after the Husker Spring Game We are in a sprint
content.text: Nebraska's head coach comments on his squad leaving spring.We're not to April yet but Nebraska spring football is complete.That doesn't mean anyone is about to hit the pause button and go take a nap."The great thing about this year is now we have five, six weeks now here of training and work," Matt Rhule said after Saturday's Spring Game. "Anyone that's banged up can get healthy. More importantly we've seen these guys now. We know what they do well, we know what they need to improve on ... So happy with the spring."‌Nebraska beat the Huskers 22-17 if you like an official score attached to your spring scrimmages.Freshman running back Jamal Rule had 119 yards on nine carries. Linebacker Derek Wacker had a game-high 10 tackles. Jacory Barney had six catches for 43 yards. Kickers were 4-of-4 on field goals. The attendance was 27,188.‌"I'm grateful for everyone that took their time to come out here and be a part of a good day. It sends a great message to our players, it sends a great message to the recruits. We have really an amazing group of recruits," said Rhule, who passed on his congratulations to Nebraska's men's basketball team for their Sweet 16 run. "But more importantly just come together and celebrate our state, celebrate our university, celebrate the football team and all the hard work that we've done."Here's everything the Husker head coach had to say.How much was today a sampling of Anthony Colandrea's ability to escape the pocket and fit some tight throws?"Yeah, he's done that all spring. As has TJ. As has Danny really, and Bode. I think when you see one guy doing it (it) kind of become contagious. It's so hard on a defense, especially quarters-based defense where you're always kind of playing three-over-two and you're doubling receivers. It's a great way to neutralize it." Some of those runs were off zone reads where there's also a throw option. "But a lot of them are just in dropback. I know in the two-minute before the half he was yelling at me because he felt like he wouldn't have been tackled when I blew the whistle. But yeah, he's got a unique gift. And he gets outside. Then I think our receivers recognize that. They're fighting to get open. Even the one, it was a naked but he got out there and he kind of bought time. He threw the ball down field and he at least gave us a shot in the end zone." It's something the Huskers are now adding to the offense, he said, "which I think really the good teams in college football have."‌You had a lot of offensive tempo. Was that something worked on more this spring?"I'm always in favor of tempo. Being a guy who's on defense I think it's a tremendous neutralizer. I just think a lot of times when they had a good first down play, I think Dana just wanted to capitalize on it and get another play ran. He's been mixing it in. It's not something I think we're going to go whole-heartedly to but I think it's something that we've done here and there. And I think it will always depend on the opponent and the game. It's something that we've been doing this spring and I think it fits the players that we have."‌There were 374 rushing yards with a 5.8 average per rush between the two teams. What did he think of the run game and the run defense?The 374 yards came on 64 rush attempts. "I think some of those were, there were two big long hits at the end. You still have to stop them but I've been really pleased with the first two defenses. I was on the BTN call I think maybe in the third quarter and I was saying ... the defense was doing a good job limiting them to three, four yards here and there. And I said there were no big hits. And after I said that Jamal took one about 80. So I might have jinxed Rob and the fellas. But I think the defense has done a real nice job."‌"I didn't see a lot of missed tackles out there, I didn't see busts ... But we have a really good offensive line. We have good tight ends, we have receivers who will block and we have backs. I've got a lot of questions about backs whether it's in here, but mainly when I go to the store or if you catch me at a bar or restaurant and people ask me about the running backs. We've kind of been on record, 'We feel like we have good backs.'" Rhule thought all the backs had some good moments. "And I think Geep and Lonnie brought some new things in. We're doing some different things, some things that Geep did at Georgia Tech which maybe diversify our run game which makes it harder to stop."‌How would you summarize Jamal Rule's spring and the day he had?"Jamal had a really good spring. What he looked like today, he looked like all spring long. He's very conscientious. He's big, he's tough, he's fast. He's got home run ability. I think the biggest thing, though, like I say is he's tough. He doesn't mind contact. He put himself through the spring in position to compete and play in the fall, which is all you can do as a freshman, right? He's got six weeks here to train, to continue to build his body up." Emmett Johnson was an anomaly in how many of the reps he took last year, Rhule added. "But I thought you saw today more of how we would probably play. 'Hey, four or five plays with this guy, get this guy in. Hey, third down, get this guy in.' And I thought you saw them all go make plays. But Jamal certainly, certainly, certainly is preparing to play this year as a freshman." ‌What did Jahsear Whittington show today and this spring?"He's a really, really explosive kid who plays really hard. I think on defense you have to have tone setters. Guys who play hard, who play tough, and other people around them it's contagious. And then they can demand it from other people and he has that ability. He's super twitched up, he's really well coached. So he's been a great addition. What I saw out there today on a day where you're not going to call a ton of sacks really because it's kind of nebulous. "Even in two-minute, end of the half, he clearly won, clearly would've had him. He yells 'sack' to me a lot. He's a Philly guy. He knows I like players who talk a little trash to me during practice and I couldn't even argue with him on that one. He's done really, really, really been a nice addition to our team." ‌Is it clear who will be the big voices on this team as you move into the next phase of the offseason?"I don't know that that's established. I think that's a good thing. I think we have a lot of guys who can do that. I think when I look at the guys out there, I think Anthony naturally has that ability, I think Jacory naturally has that ability. Luke is a guy that people follow, Justin Evans is a guy that people follow. On defense there's guys like Jahsear who are just going to lead with their effort. Guys like Riley who people respect, Cam Lenhardt. "So I think we have a great balance right now of guys who have been here, been in the program: Understand what it means to play at Nebraska. How we want to honor our fans and the legacy here and the stadium we play in there. "And at the same time guys who come in who bring some juice, who bring some leadership qualities. But I think right now we're less looking for leadership and more looking for good football to be quite honest. We're looking for production, we're looking for grit. Gritty guys who show up every day and want to be part of a brotherhood. But most importantly they want to go out and execute and play hard."‌How'd you come out of the spring health-wise?"We lost Jacob Bower early on to a non-contact knee. Nyziah (Hunter) pulled his hamstring but nothing real serious. Dexter Foster, I don't think he did anything today, because he has just a bruise. But in terms of long term, surgical type injuries, really it's just Jacob Bower we're coming out of (spring) with."‌What did Derek Wacker show today and this spring?"Derek's a really good football player. He helped us a ton on special teams as a freshman. He's fast, he's tough, he's athletic. I saw him make some key plays. The biggest thing is to me is he made key tackles on a back one-on-one who is a legitimate college football Power 4 back. That's what you go out there to do. You go out there to prove you can play in that environment versus good players. Happy for him, he's done it all spring and he'll continue to fight to be a contributing member of the team."‌What did you learn about what you have on the O-line?"We have a bunch of really good players. You add in (Tyler) Knaak and (Sam) Sledge who are guys we feel really good about (to the first five of Elijah Pritchett, Paul Mubenga, Justin Evans, Brendan Black and Tree Babalade). You bring back Gunnar Gotulla (in the summer). And you have some other injured guys, young guys like Gibson Pyle and (Nolan) Fennessy and JuJul Marks who they'll be back at some point. "I think we have a lot of good depth. A lot of good guys that are young that we think will be starters here ... But I think when you talk about your first five, and your first eight, we feel good about where we are."‌Big news for Anthony JonesHe wasn't out there today. He had a wonderful excuse. His wife had a baby yesterday morning. Jones texted the coach at 8:30 on Friday that a future pass rushing baby boy had just entered the world. "He's been really, really a great addition to us. You look at his story, his journey, five schools in five years. And maybe at first to be honest that was a red flag. Then you start to see the whys. 'Hey, coach left, coach left.' He has been fantastic in terms of his maturity. I just told him, 'Please stay home and be a dad today.' We didn't need him out there."‌It seems like Colandrea and Jacory Barney have a connection out there. Has that been consistent this spring?"I think Anthony does a great job getting the ball to everybody. It's third-and-5 today he hits Luke on the crossing route. He finds the backs. He went deep a couple times to Kwazi. It was good for Anthony to see what the stadium wind was like ... Quinn Clark has had a really good spring, Cortez has had a really good spring. I think we like our both our starting receivers and the guys that will rotate in. And some other guys that will continue to develop. "And I think the thing about Anthony, especially the way he plays, he's playing 100 mph. He's going to go through his progression. If there's any pressure he's going to get outside the pocket. He's going to just try to make plays and he's going to trust the guys to make the plays."‌What do these next five, six weeks look like?"We go back to training. Sometimes when the Spring Game was later, kind of after that you kind of recover. We are in a sprint. And it's different for each person maybe right now. For some guys, hey, get a little bit stronger; hey, you got to get a little bit healthier; hey, you got to lose some weight, gain some weight. So it will be very prescriptive to each person. I think that's the best part of what we did. We didn't do anything without studying it really hard – really hard." Added Rhule, "We'll be back in there Monday morning, starting with a 7:30 team meeting. Back to work."LOOK: More than 50 recruits roll through Lincoln for Nebraska's Red White Game, Gallery 2More recruits who were on the sidelines for Nebraska's Red-White game on Saturday.
